title: Specs Sidecar Shared Definitions
description: The vocabulary the two authored sidecar documents share: the concern, platform, verification and pointer sets, plus the header both open with. Referenced by supplemental.schema.json and guidelines.schema.json rather than restated in either. A sidecar is authored by hand — no run writes one — so it carries no metadata.source and records authorship and review status instead. (ADR-118)

SidecarMeta.description: Authorship and review status for a sidecar document as a whole. Every member is optional; status is the member that earns the block, because nothing else distinguishes a proposal from ratified guidance.

concern.description: The subject this document covers, restating what the containing directory names — a foundation concern at the foundation scope, a component name at the component scope.

status.description: Where the document sits in its review cycle.

oneOf.description: Drafted and awaiting a ratifier; its statements are not yet the system's position.
Reviewed and adopted; its statements are the system's position.
Superseded or withdrawn; kept for the record and not to be followed.

author.description: Who authored it. Duplicates git history, and is here for a reader who will not consult git.

updated.description: When it was last revised, as YYYY-MM-DD. Hand-maintained, so it can go stale.

sources.description: The generated reports this document was synthesized from, as workspace-relative paths.

Platform.description: A platform an entry is scoped to. Each value names an emission target: the two web frameworks this system emits, the two native platforms whose single sanctioned framework makes the platform name sufficient, and a group covering both web targets at once.

oneOf.description: Lit web components, emitted by webcomponents-from-specs.
Both web targets at once; expands to react and webcomponents, and may not be named beside either leaf.
Android, as Kotlin with Jetpack Compose.

Platforms.description: The platforms an entry applies to. Absent means every platform. Because web expands to both web targets, naming it beside react or webcomponents states one thing twice and is rejected.

CheckedBy.description: How a statement is checked. The checks member names what does the checking, and is required whenever this is automated.

oneOf.description: A test or lint rule decides it, with no human reading required.
A tool surfaces candidates and a human judges them.
A human decides it, with no tool involved.

Pointer.description: A reference to one thing, either inside this workspace or outside it. Exactly one member is present: to names something the workspace holds, href names something it does not. Resolution of to is DSPEC-57.

to.description: What this points at inside the workspace — a token in analysis/foundations.yaml, a component, or an item within one.

href.description: What this points at outside the workspace, as an absolute URL.

Pointers.description: One or more references to things, inside this workspace or outside it.

Ref.description: A pointer that states its relationship explicitly, for the relationships that have no field of their own.

to.description: What this points at inside the workspace.

href.description: What this points at outside the workspace, as an absolute URL.

rel.description: What the target is to the thing carrying this ref.

oneOf.description: The target states the same thing at another scope, and the duplication is deliberate.
The target is an issue or document bearing on this, without restating it.
The target is the code or package this comes from.
The target is the design file or frame this comes from.
The target is a running example of this.
